Let \(\mathscr E=\sigma(E_0)\).  By the definition of \(z_0\), the vector \(z_0=\mathbb E_P[Z_j\mid E_0]\) is \(\mathscr E\)-measurable.  Thus adjoining \(z_0\) to the conditioning field generated by \(E_0\) does not change any conditional expectation below.  By \texttt{def:target} and linearity of conditional expectation,
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0,E_0]
-\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} and the definition of \(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\) give
\[
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0].
\tag{2}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-transport} gives, for each cohort,
\[
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
=m_s(z_{0s}).
\tag{3}
\]
Substitution of (2)--(3) into (1) proves
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-regression} identifies \(m_s(x)\) separately as the observed-law conditional mean of an untreated pseudo-event response at \(X_{st}=x\).  Hence consistency and event transport prove the equality between the causal contrast and the observed-law functional; it is not introduced as a definition of the causal target.

Fix a successful cohort \(s\), abbreviate \(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\) by \(\bar B_s\), and hold \(\gamma\in\mathbb R^{q_r}\) fixed.  The event part of the criterion in \texttt{def:fwl-regression} satisfies the exact sum-of-squares identity
\[
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\theta-e_0^\top\gamma)^2
=\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\bar B_s)^2
+(\bar B_s-\theta-e_0^\top\gamma)^2.
\tag{4}
\]
Consequently, for fixed \(\gamma\), the unique minimizing event coefficient is
\[
\theta=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^\top\gamma.
\tag{5}
\]
At (5), the event criterion is independent of \(\gamma\).  Up to the first, constant term in (4), the profiled criterion is therefore
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-b_r(u_{st})^\top\gamma\}^2,
\tag{6}
\]
which is precisely the historical weighted least-squares problem in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  Passage of the normalized-shape test implies \(L_s>0\) and
\[
G_s\succeq c_GL_sI_{q_r}\succ0.
\]
Thus (6) has the unique minimizer \(\widehat\gamma_s\), and profiling gives
\[
\widehat\theta_s=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s.
\tag{7}
\]
Using the definitions of \(\widehat m_s\), \(\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}\), and \(\widehat\tau\), on every sample for which all selected fits exist,
\[
\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s)
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s)
=\widehat\tau.
\]

Fix a regular conditional experiment given \(E_0\), put \(D=Sd\), and, for any class member, define only in this proof
\[
Y=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_1-z_0).
\]
The definitions of \(z_0\) and \(\Sigma\), together with \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, give
\[
\mathbb E_P[YY^\top\mid E_0]=I_D.
\]
Taking traces and applying Jensen's inequality to \(\|Y\|_2^2\) yield
\[
\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^2\mid E_0]=\operatorname{tr}(I_D)=D,
\qquad
D^2\le\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^4\mid E_0]\le B,
\tag{42}
\]
where the last inequality is \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}.  Therefore \(B\ge D^2\) is necessary for nonemptiness, and the class is empty when \(B<D^2\).  Strict inequality is not a consequence of nonemptiness.

We first describe a causal completion common to all asserted channels.  Let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\}.
\]
Choose the event path in the admissible part of \(\mathcal Z_+\) and away from the cube boundary.  All response kernels used below have support in a fixed compact subinterval of \((0,B)\), and all Bernoulli mixing probabilities are in \([\eta,1-\eta]\) for some fixed \(0<\eta<1/2\).  If \(p,p+v\in[\eta,1-\eta]\), two differentiations of binary relative entropy give
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p+v,p)\le C_\eta v^2.
\tag{43}
\]
Indeed, the first derivative vanishes at \(v=0\), while the second derivative is uniformly bounded on that compact interval.

Draw event outcomes independently of \(\mathscr X\).  Conditional on \(\mathscr X\), draw bounded historical response paths independently across \((s,i)\), from kernels that may vary with \((s,i)\) but satisfy
\[
\mathbb E_P[Q_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=m_s(X_{st}).
\]
Then, with \(\varepsilon_{sti}=Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{44}
\]
Complete the unobserved event-date untreated potential outcomes so that their cohort-average conditional means equal \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  Set the observed and historical potential outcomes according to \texttt{ass:consistency} and \texttt{ass:historical-consistency}; make historical potential outcomes invariant to event treatment and every potential outcome invariant to other units' assignments.  Take \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  These choices give limited anticipation, no spillovers, event transport, and the two restrictions in \texttt{def:full-design-centered-class}.  Because all wealth values are strictly between zero and \(B\), they can be represented by \texttt{def:buyhold-level} using a sufficiently small positive initial wealth and returns strictly above \(-1\).  In each channel the donor sample is conditionally independent of the panel and conditionally independent and identically distributed.

For every compatible \(B\ge D^2\), the three non-donor channels use the same donor marginal.  Conditional on \(E_0\), let
\[
U\sim\operatorname{Unif}\{\pm\sqrt D\,e_k:1\le k\le D\},
\qquad Z_j=z_0+U_j,
\]
with independent copies \(U_j\).  Symmetry gives
\[
\mathbb E[U\mid E_0]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E[UU^\top\mid E_0]=I_D,
\qquad
\mathbb E[\|U\|_2^4\mid E_0]=D^2\le B.
\tag{45}
\]
Since \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), (45) verifies both donor envelopes even at \(B=D^2\).

For the treated channel put
\[
V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=R_{\mathrm{tr}},
\qquad
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}}.
\]
Because \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), one has \(|v_s|\le c_0n_s^{-1/2}\le c_0\).  Choose \(c_0\) small enough that every event-response probability remains in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).  Change only the treated event-response probability in cohort \(s\) by \(v_s\); keep the untreated surfaces and all other observed laws fixed.  Absorbing the fixed response-support separation into constants, \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and (43) give
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{tr}}}(z_0)-
\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{tr}}}(z_0)|
=cV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{tr}},P_{0,\mathrm{tr}})
\le C\sum_s n_sv_s^2\le Cc_0^2.
\tag{46}
\]

For the smoothing channel choose \(s_*\) maximizing
\(\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\), and set
\[
b=c_b(Tn_{s_*})^{-1/(2\lambda+d)},
\]
where fixed \(c_b>0\) keeps the bump support inside the cube.  Perturb only this cohort by
\[
m_{s_*,1}(x)-m_{s_*,0}(x)
=c_1b^\lambda\psi((x-z_{0s_*})/b),
\tag{47}
\]
where \(\psi\) is a fixed smooth compactly supported bump with \(\psi(0)=1\).  Use a bounded carrier with a nonzero covariance-standardized affine slope when \(\lambda>1\), and an asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp when \(0<\lambda\le1\), scaled within the response, H\"older, and two-sided-modulus envelopes.  For \(\delta\le b\), the increment of (47) over a displacement of standardized size \(\delta\) is at most \(Cc_1\delta^\kappa\); for \(\delta>b\), boundedness of the bump and \(b^\lambda\le C\delta^\kappa\) give the same bound.  Thus sufficiently small \(c_1\) preserves both sides of the local modulus.  Since \(S\) is fixed,
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)-
\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)|^2
&=c\pi_{s_*}^2b^{2\lambda}\\
&\ge c\sum_s\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
=cR_{\mathrm{sm}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{48}
\]
Use an independent uniform historical design.  Its probability of meeting the bump support is at most \(Cb^d\).  Conditional product structure, (43), and integration over the design yield
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{sm}},P_{0,\mathrm{sm}})
\le CTn_{s_*}b^{2\lambda+d}\le C.
\tag{49}
\]
The perturbation constant can be decreased so that the last constant is arbitrarily small while the separation remains a fixed positive multiple of the displayed rate.

For the spacing channel, \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction} supplies laws using the common donor marginal (45) such that
\[
\int\min\{dP_{0,\mathrm{sp}},dP_{1,\mathrm{sp}}\}
\ge a_{\mathrm{sp}}>0,
\qquad
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)-
\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{50}
\]
Only positive testing affinity is asserted or needed for this channel.

It remains to construct the donor channel, for which fix the strict slack \(B-D^2>0\).  Choose \(0<\xi<D\) so that
\[
D^2+\xi^2<B,
\]
put \(r_-=(D-\xi)^{1/2}\) and \(r_+=(D+\xi)^{1/2}\), and choose two sufficiently close admissible interior centers
\[
z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\mu e_1,
\qquad
\mu=c_2N^{-1/2},
\]
where \(e_1\) is a coordinate direction in one cohort block.  Use the common finite support
\[
\mathcal A=\{z^{(0)}\pm r_-e_k,
z^{(0)}\pm r_+e_k:1\le k\le D\}.
\]
Under law zero, give every atom probability \(1/(4D)\).  Its mean is \(z^{(0)}\), its covariance is \(I_D\), and its standardized fourth moment is
\[
\frac{r_-^4+r_+^4}{2}=D^2+\xi^2<B.
\tag{51}
\]
Under law one leave all probabilities except the four atoms in direction \(e_1\) unchanged.  With
\[
a_N=\frac{\mu}{2r_-},
\qquad
b_N=\frac{\mu^2}{2\xi},
\]
replace the probabilities at \(z^{(0)}+r_-e_1\), \(z^{(0)}-r_-e_1\), \(z^{(0)}+r_+e_1\), and \(z^{(0)}-r_+e_1\), respectively, by
\[
\frac1{4D}-\frac{b_N}{2}+a_N,
\quad
\frac1{4D}-\frac{b_N}{2}-a_N,
\quad
\frac1{4D}+\frac{b_N}{2},
\quad
\frac1{4D}+\frac{b_N}{2}.
\tag{52}
\]
For sufficiently small fixed \(c_2\), depending on the fixed slack through \(\xi\), all probabilities in (52) are positive for every \(N\), and they sum to their baseline total.  Direct calculation gives
\[
\mathbb E_1[Z_j-z^{(0)}]=2a_Nr_-e_1=\mu e_1,
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E_1[(Z_j-z^{(0)})(Z_j-z^{(0)})^\top]
=I_D+b_N(r_+^2-r_-^2)e_1e_1^\top
=I_D+\mu^2e_1e_1^\top.
\]
Thus \(\mathbb E_1Z_j=z^{(1)}\) and
\(\operatorname{Var}_1(Z_j\mid E_0)=I_D\) exactly.  The standardized fourth moment is a continuous function of the finite probability vector and \(\mu\).  By (51), the fixed strict slack permits a further reduction of \(c_2\) such that this moment remains below \(B\) under both laws.  This is the only point at which \(B>D^2\), rather than compatibility alone, is used.

The baseline probabilities are bounded below, and the changes in (52) are \(O(\mu)\).  Taylor expansion of \(x\log(x/y)\) on a compact subinterval of \((0,1)\) gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{don}},P_{0,\mathrm{don}})
\le CN(a_N^2+b_N^2)
\le CN\mu^2\le Cc_2^2.
\tag{53}
\]
For \(\kappa=1\), choose the weighted regression carrier to have nonzero linear slope in direction \(e_1\).  For \(0<\kappa=\lambda<1\), use in the selected cohort the common surface
\[
x\longmapsto c_3+c_4|e_1^\top(x-z^{(0)})|^\lambda
+c_5|e_1^\top(x-z^{(1)})|^\lambda,
\qquad c_4,c_5>0,\quad c_4\ne c_5.
\tag{54}
\]
Fixed rescaling places (54) inside the response and H\"older envelopes.  At \(z^{(0)}\), displacement away from \(z^{(1)}\) increases both cusp terms; at \(z^{(1)}\), displacement in the opposite outward direction does the same.  These admissible one-coordinate displacements give the lower modulus, while the H\"older inequality gives the upper modulus.  Therefore both centers satisfy the maintained two-sided condition.  Evaluation at the two centers gives
\[
\left|\sum_s\pi_s\{m_s(z_s^{(1)})-m_s(z_s^{(0)})\}\right|
\ge c\mu^\kappa=cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{55}
\]
Keep the historical observed law, the regression surface, and the observed event mean fixed across the donor laws.  Under law \(\ell\), complete untreated event outcomes with cohort means \(m_s(z_s^{(\ell)})\).  The identification equality in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} turns (55) into squared target separation at least \(cN^{-\kappa}=cR_{\mathrm{don}}\).

For completeness, bounded divergence gives positive affinity without importing a separate theorem.  Let \(A=\{dP_1/dP_0\ge1\}\), \(p=P_1(A)\), and \(q=P_0(A)\).  The log-sum inequality, obtained directly from convexity of \(x\log x\), gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)\ge\operatorname{kl}(p,q).
\]
Twice differentiating \(\operatorname{kl}(q+u,q)\) and using
\(q(1-q)\le1/4\) gives \(\operatorname{kl}(p,q)\ge2(p-q)^2\).  Since \(p-q=\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\),
\[
\int\min\{dP_0,dP_1\}
=1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\ge1-\{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2\}^{1/2}.
\tag{56}
\]
Decreasing \(c_0,c_1,c_2\) makes (56) uniformly positive for the treated, smoothing, and, only under strict slack, donor pairs; (50) handles spacing.  The causal completion following (44) verifies that every pair is induced by a regular conditional law of the complete causal panel.  The query is chosen in \(\mathcal Z_+\), so each law assigns it conditional probability one, which is at least \(c_X\).  Equations (42)--(56) prove all four channel assertions when \(B>D^2\).  When \(B=D^2\), equations (45)--(50) prove exactly the treated, smoothing, and spacing assertions, with a common donor marginal and without a donor converse.

The compatibility calculation (42) in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} proves that the class is empty for \(B<D^2\).  Suppose first that \(B>D^2\).  For a channel \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\), take \((P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\) from that lemma, write their conditional target values as \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), and put \(\Delta_q=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Their conditional testing affinity is at least a fixed \(a_q>0\), and \(\Delta_q^2\ge cR_q\).  For any observed-data estimator \(\widetilde\tau\), the events
\[
E'_0=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_0|\ge\Delta_q/2\},
\qquad
E'_1=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_1|\ge\Delta_q/2\}
\]
cover the sample space by the triangle inequality.  Integration against the overlap measure gives
\[
P_{0,q}(E'_0\mid E_0)+P_{1,q}(E'_1\mid E_0)\ge a_q.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_\ell)^2\mid E_0]
\ge\frac{a_q\Delta_q^2}{8}\ge cR_q.
\tag{57}
\]
Maximizing over the four channels and using
\(R_{\star,\beta}=\max_qR_q\) proves the strict-slack lower bound.  The donor-channel constant may depend on \(B-D^2\), as stated.  When \(B=D^2\), the boundary part of \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} supplies (57) only for \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp}\}\).  Maximizing over precisely these channels proves the displayed three-channel lower bound and makes no donor converse.

The upper bound is common to both nonempty regimes.  Let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,\ t\le T\},
\]
and condition on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  On successful fits, \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and the linear representation in \texttt{def:honest-interval} give
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=U_{\mathrm{evt}}-U_{\mathrm{hist}}-B_{\mathrm{LP}}-B_{\mathrm{don}},
\tag{58}
\]
where
\[
U_{\mathrm{evt}}=
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\},
\]
\[
U_{\mathrm{hist}}=
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\pi_s
\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti},
\]
\[
B_{\mathrm{LP}}=
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\left\{\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{sti}m_s(X_{st})
-m_s(\widetilde z_s)\right\},
\]
and
\[
B_{\mathrm{don}}=
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
The two full-design restrictions center the first two sums under this conditioning; donor independence permits the donor sample to be adjoined.  Conditional cross-unit independence and the bounded response range imply
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{evt}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
\le B^2\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=B^2R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{59}
\]
Treating one unit's entire response history as one cluster and applying \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{hist}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
\le B^2\sum_{s,i}\left[\pi_s\sum_t|a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le B^2c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{60}
\]
No temporal outcome restriction or identical response law is used.

Let \(C_K\) bound the Euclidean radius of the support of \(K\).  Whenever \(w_{st}>0\),
\(\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2\le C_Kh_s\).  Polynomial reproduction, the H\"older Taylor remainder, and the deterministic absolute-weight bound give
\[
|B_{\mathrm{LP}}|\le C\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz across the fixed cohorts and \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(2\lambda\), first conditional on \(\widetilde z_s\) and then integrated over the donors,
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{LP}}^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}+N^{-\lambda}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta},
\tag{61}
\]
because \(N^{-\lambda}\le N^{-\kappa}\).

For donor control define only in this proof
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{N}Y_j.
\]
Conditional donor replication gives independent mean-zero vectors with
\(\mathbb E_P[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Expanding \(\|W_N\|_2^4\), all terms containing a singleton sample index vanish.  The all-equal terms and the three pairings yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
&=\frac1N\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-\frac1N\right)
\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\}\\
&\le\frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)=M_4(N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{62}
\]
Thus
\(\mathbb E_P[\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2^4\mid E_0]\le CN^{-2}\).
Euclidean projection onto the cube cannot increase distance from \(z_0\), and ellipticity gives
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2.
\tag{63}
\]
On the event where the left side is at most \(\delta_0\), the upper local-modulus inequality bounds \(|B_{\mathrm{don}}|^2\) by a constant times that norm to power \(2\kappa\).  Lyapunov's inequality and (62) give expectation at most \(CN^{-\kappa}\).  On the complement, \(|B_{\mathrm{don}}|\le B\), while Markov's inequality and (62) bound its probability by \(O(N^{-2})\).  Since \(0<\kappa\le1\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{don}}^2\mid E_0]
\le CN^{-\kappa}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{64}
\]
This argument uses only the upper fourth-moment premise and remains valid at \(B=D^2\).

Every successful intercept satisfies
\[
|\widehat m_s|\le B\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|\le Bc_G^{-1/2},
\]
and a failed intercept contribution is zero.  Hence the squared estimation error is bounded by a fixed constant on the bad sample.  The bad-sample probability in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} makes its contribution at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\) along the asserted arrays.  Combining (58)--(64) with
\((x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4)^2\le4\sum_{j=1}^{4}x_j^2\) proves
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le CR_{\star,\beta}.
\tag{65}
\]
The estimator is observed-data measurable and does not use unknown \(\Sigma\), so (65) also upper-bounds the minimax infimum.  Combining it with the strict-slack or equality-boundary lower argument proves every displayed bracket and the claimed case split.

The compatibility calculation (42) in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} shows that \(B<D^2\) gives an empty class.  Fix a compatible envelope \(B\ge D^2\), let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,\ t\le T\},
\]
and condition first on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  On each successful fit, polynomial reproduction from \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control}, applied to the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_s\), gives
\[
\left|e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s-m_s(\widetilde z_s)
-\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}|a_{sti}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{66}
\]
After cohort weighting, the right side is exactly \(A_L\).

Define the historical unit-cluster variables
\[
\mathsf H_{si}=\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering} and donor independence give
\[
\mathbb E_P[\mathsf H_{si}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]=0.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes these variables independent over \((s,i)\) under this conditioning.  Because \(0\le Q_{sti}\le B\), the conditional range length of \(\mathsf H_{si}\) is at most
\[
c_{si}=B\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}|a_{sti}|.
\]
If a conditionally centered random variable \(U\) lies in an interval of length \(c\), convexity of \(x\mapsto e^{vx}\) bounds its exponential moment by the endpoint mixture having the same mean.  Direct differentiation of the logarithm of that two-point mixture gives
\[
\mathbb E[e^{vU}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]\le e^{v^2c^2/8}.
\tag{67}
\]
Multiplying (67) over independent unit clusters, applying exponential Markov inequality, optimizing over \(v>0\), and repeating for \(-U\) yield
\[
P_P\left\{
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathsf H_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{68}
\]
Thus each unit's full calendar history is one bounded cluster; no within-unit temporal restriction is used.

Similarly define
\[
\mathsf E_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} centers \(\mathsf E_{si}\) given \((\mathscr X,E_0)\); donor independence preserves this centering after donors are adjoined, and cross-unit independence gives conditional independence.  Their conditional range lengths are at most \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  The same calculation gives
\[
P_P\left\{
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathsf E_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{69}
\]
A union bound combines (68)--(69), without requiring independence between one unit's historical path and event outcome.

For donor calibration define only in this proof
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{N}Y_j.
\]
The conditional fourth-moment expansion in (62) gives
\[
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
\le\frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)=M_4(N).
\tag{70}
\]
Define the proof event \(\mathcal D_N=\{\|W_N\|_2\le q_N\}\).  Markov's inequality and the definition of \(q_N\) imply
\[
P_P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)
\le\frac{M_4(N)}{q_N^4}=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{71}
\]
Projection onto \([0,1]^{Sd}\) cannot increase Euclidean distance from \(z_0\), because \(z_0\) lies in that cube.  The covariance eigenvalue bounds therefore give, on \(\mathcal D_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\widetilde z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\bar Z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,q_N/\sqrt N
=\delta_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{72}
\]
On the good event in \texttt{def:honest-interval}, \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\).  The upper half of \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} and (72) imply
\[
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_N^\kappa=A_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{73}
\]

Let \(\mathcal G\) be the selector-and-radius good event in \texttt{def:honest-interval}; it is measurable with respect to \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j))\).  On \(\mathcal G^c\), the fallback interval is \([-B,B]\).  Every potential-outcome contrast has conditional mean in \([-B,B]\), and the positive cohort weights sum to one, so \(\tau_n(z_0)\in[-B,B]\).  On \(\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N\), \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, (66), and (73) decompose the estimation error into the event fluctuation, the historical fluctuation, and two terms bounded by \(A_L\) and \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Hence noncoverage implies failure of (68) or (69).  Iterated conditioning gives, for every positive sample size,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_P\{\tau_n(z_0)\notin C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
&\le P_P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)\\
&\quad+\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf1_{\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N}
P_P\{\text{historical failure or event failure}
\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\}
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]\\
&\le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}
+\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}=\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{74}
\]
No selector-tail probability enters (74), so coverage is exact and finite-sample for every compatible envelope, including \(B=D^2\).  Intersecting the untruncated interval with \([-B,B]\) cannot remove the target because the target itself lies in that set.

For expected length, \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives on every successful fit
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\le B\left\{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}})c_G^{-1}
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}})
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{75}
\]
The support of \(K\) and the same deterministic weight bound give
\[
A_L\le C\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\]
Apply \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(\lambda\), conditionally on the projected donor center, and use Cauchy--Schwarz across the fixed cohorts.  Then
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[A_L\mathbf1_{\mathcal G}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}
+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}+N^{-\lambda/2}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{76}
\]
Since \(D,B,\alpha\) are fixed, (70) implies \(q_N\le C\), and hence
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}\le CN^{-\kappa/2}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}.
\tag{77}
\]
The selector lemma gives \(P_P(\mathcal G^c\mid E_0)\le CR_{\star,\beta}\) along the asserted arrays.  The fallback length is at most \(2B\), eventually \(R_{\star,\beta}\le R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\), and \(\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\le2H_\alpha\) on \(\mathcal G\).  Equations (75)--(77) therefore prove, in either compatible regime with its independently quantified upper constant,
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_\alpha^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{78}
\]

It remains to establish the expected-length converse.  In the treated, smoothing, and donor constructions of \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}, the perturbation constants may be decreased while remaining fixed in the array.  Equations (46), (49), and (53), together with (56), then make the corresponding affinities arbitrarily close to one while preserving separation by a positive constant times \(R_q^{1/2}\).  In the spacing construction, decreasing the fixed rare-block probability constant \(c_p\) makes the no-active-block probability in (39) arbitrarily close to one while preserving a positive fixed multiple of \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}\).  Therefore, for fixed \(\alpha<1/2\), the pair constants can be selected so that every available channel affinity \(A_q\) exceeds \(2\alpha+a_0\) for some fixed \(a_0>0\).  In the donor channel these constants may depend on the strict slack \(B-D^2\).

Let \(I\) be finite-sample conditionally honest, let \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) be a channel pair's targets, and let \(\mu_q=P_{0,q}\wedge P_{1,q}\) be the conditional overlap measure.  Uniform conditional honesty gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_q\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}
&\ge\mu_q(\Omega)
-P_{0,q}\{\theta_0\notin I\mid E_0\}
-P_{1,q}\{\theta_1\notin I\mid E_0\}\\
&\ge A_q-2\alpha\ge a_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{79}
\]
On this event, \(\operatorname{length}(I)\ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Consequently,
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge a_0|\theta_1-\theta_0|
\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\tag{80}
\]
For \(B>D^2\), maximizing (80) over all four channels gives
\(c_{\alpha,>}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\), with dependence on the fixed slack allowed.  At \(B=D^2\), apply (80) only to the treated, smoothing, and spacing pairs supplied by the boundary part of \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}; this yields
\[
c_{\alpha,=}\{R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\}^{1/2}
\]
and asserts no donor converse.  If an interval sequence is only uniformly asymptotically conditionally honest, then for each \(\epsilon>0\) both noncoverage probabilities are eventually at most \(\alpha+\epsilon\).  Choosing \(\epsilon<a_0/4\) replaces the final lower bound in (79) by at least \(a_0/2\), proving the same rates.  Equations (74), (78), and (80), with the stated case split, prove every assertion.

Under the first specialization, \(S=1\) and \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\) imply \(\pi_1=1\).  The identifying equality in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and the restriction \(m_1(x)=x+\Delta_0\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_n(z_0)
&=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_1(z_{01})\\
&=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-z_{01}-\Delta_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{81}
\]
When the scalar proxy is the event cohort's baseline outcome, \(z_{01}\) is its conditional baseline mean.  When \(\Delta_0\) is the untreated cohort-average post-minus-baseline mean change, (81) is treated post minus treated baseline minus the untreated post-minus-baseline change.  This is the canonical conditional finite-cohort two-period difference-in-differences contrast.

For the second specialization define the cohort effect
\[
\tau_s=\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)-B_{si}(0)\mid z_0,E_0].
\]
Homogeneity across cohorts means that \(\tau_s=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}\) for every \(s\).  By \texttt{def:target} and \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\),
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\tau_s
=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}.
\tag{82}
\]
The stipulated absence of carry-over beyond \(h=0\) makes this common terminal-level contrast the contemporaneous finite-cohort treatment effect on the level-wealth path in \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.  This last causal interpretation uses the stated specialization; it does not follow from the aggregation identity alone.

Fix a successful cohort and suppress its index.  Write \(\mathsf L=L_s\), \(G=G_s\), and
\[
v_{ti}=w_{st}^{1/2}b_r(u_{st}).
\]
Then
\[
G=\sum_{t,i}v_{ti}v_{ti}^\top,
\qquad
a_{sti}=w_{st}^{1/2}e_0^\top G^{-1}v_{ti}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz and the definition of \(G\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|
&\le
\left\{\sum_{t,i}(e_0^\top G^{-1}v_{ti})^2\right\}^{1/2}
\left\{\sum_{t,i}w_{st}\right\}^{1/2}\\
&=\{e_0^\top G^{-1}GG^{-1}e_0\}^{1/2}\mathsf L^{1/2}
=\{\mathsf Le_0^\top G^{-1}e_0\}^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
The selector requires \(G/\mathsf L\succeq c_GI_{q_r}\), so
\[
G^{-1}\preceq(c_G\mathsf L)^{-1}I_{q_r}.
\]
In the declared monomial basis, \(e_0=b_r(0)\) is the constant-monomial coordinate and \(\|e_0\|_2=1\).  Hence
\[
\mathsf Le_0^\top G^{-1}e_0\le c_G^{-1}.
\tag{9}
\]
Equations (8)--(9) prove the first displayed chain in the lemma.

For fixed \((s,t)\), neither \(u_{st}\) nor \(w_{st}\) depends on the replicated-unit index, and
\[
G_s=n_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_{st}b_r(u_{st})b_r(u_{st})^\top.
\]
Therefore \(a_{sti}\) is constant in \(i\).  Equations (8)--(9) imply
\[
\sum_t|a_{sti}|\le\frac{c_G^{-1/2}}{n_s}.
\tag{10}
\]
It follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\left[\pi_s\sum_t|a_{sti}|\right]^2
&\le\sum_{s=1}^{S}n_s
\left(\frac{\pi_sc_G^{-1/2}}{n_s}\right)^2\\
&=c_G^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
=c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]

It remains to verify the bias assertion.  The normal equations and invertibility of \(G_s\) reproduce every polynomial \(p\) of total degree at most \(r\):
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{sti}p(u_{st})=p(0).
\tag{12}
\]
Indeed, if \(p(u)=c^\top b_r(u)\), the left side of (12) is
\(e_0^\top G_s^{-1}G_sc=e_0^\top c=p(0)\).  Subtract the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_s\).  The remainder convention in \texttt{ass:holder-smoothness}, with \(r=\lceil\lambda\rceil-1\), gives
\[
|m_s(x)-T_{r,\widetilde z_s}m_s(x)|
\le C_{r,d}L\|x-\widetilde z_s\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{13}
\]
Multiplying (13) by \(|a_{sti}|\), summing over \((t,i)\), and then weighting by \(\pi_s\) bounds the absolute aggregate Taylor remainder by
\[
C_{r,d}L\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}|a_{sti}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2^\lambda=A_L.
\]
Every step is deterministic on a successful fit, and no upper bound on \(L_s\) has been used.

Fix a cohort \(s\) and condition throughout on \((E_0,\widetilde z_s=z)\).  By \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, adjoining \(\widetilde z_s\), which is measurable with respect to the donors and \(E_0\), does not change the conditional law of the historical design.  By \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}, the stacked design process alone obeys the geometric absolute-regularity bound; no historical outcome process is used in this proof.

For \(z\in[0,1]^d\) and \(0<h\le1\), define
\[
\ell_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h),
\qquad
\Phi_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)^\top.
\]
Bounded support of \(K\), the upper density bound, and the change of variables \(x=z+hu\) give a fixed \(C_0<\infty\) such that
\[
\mathbb E_P[\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\mid E_0]\le C_0h^d.
\tag{14}
\]
There is also a uniform lower bound.  Choose \(\eta>0\) and \(k_0>0\) such that \(K(u)\ge k_0\) on \([ -\eta,\eta]^d\).  For every \(z\) and \(h\le1\), the set \(h^{-1}([0,1]^d-z)\cap[-\eta,\eta]^d\) contains one of a fixed finite collection of orthant boxes with all side lengths bounded below.  On any such box a nonzero polynomial \(v^\top b_r(u)\) cannot vanish almost everywhere.  Compactness of the unit sphere in the fixed-dimensional space \(\mathbb R^{q_r}\), followed by the lower density bound, gives \(c_0>0\) such that, uniformly in \(s,t,z,h\),
\[
c_0h^d\le\mathbb E_P[\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[v^\top\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st})v\mid E_0]
\ge c_0h^d\|v\|_2^2.
\tag{15}
\]
Choose the fixed procedural threshold so that \(0<c_G<c_0/(4C_0)\).

Let \(A_0>2\lambda/d+2\), and put
\[
b_T=\lceil C_\beta\log(T\vee2)\rceil.
\]
The fixed constant \(C_\beta\) can be chosen so that
\[
T\beta_0\rho_0^{b_T}\le T^{-A_0}.
\tag{16}
\]
Partition \(\{1,\ldots,T\}\) into consecutive blocks of length at most \(b_T\), and split the blocks into odd and even subfamilies.  Within either subfamily, successive blocks are separated by a whole block.  From the definition of the absolute-regularity coefficient, the conditional joint distribution of two sigma-fields separated by \(b_T\) has total-variation distance at most \(\beta_P(b_T\mid E_0)\) from the product of its marginals.  Applying this fact successively and telescoping the resulting signed measures shows that the law of either parity subfamily is within
\[
C(T/b_T)\beta_P(b_T\mid E_0)\le CT^{-A_0}
\tag{17}
\]
in total variation of the product of its conditional block marginals.  This is a direct finite induction: at each step, replacing the conditional law of the next separated block by its marginal changes the joint law by at most the corresponding absolute-regularity coefficient, and total variation obeys the triangle inequality.

Let \(F\) be either \(\ell_{z,h}\) or \(v^\top\Phi_{z,h}v\) with \(\|v\|_2=1\), and let \(W_g\) be the sum of \(F(X_{st})\) over block \(g\) in one parity.  Boundedness of \(K\) and of \(b_r\) on the support of \(K\) implies
\[
0\le W_g\le Cb_T,
\qquad
W_g^2\le Cb_TW_g.
\]
Under the product law from (17), the variables \(W_g\) are independent.  Equations (14)--(15) imply
\[
\sum_g\operatorname{Var}(W_g)
\le\sum_g\mathbb E[W_g^2]
\le Cb_TTh^d.
\tag{18}
\]
For \(V_g=W_g-\mathbb EW_g\), expansion of the exponential series and \(|V_g|\le Cb_T\) give, for \(0<\theta<(Cb_T)^{-1}\),
\[
\mathbb E e^{\theta V_g}
\le\exp\left\{
\frac{\theta^2\operatorname{Var}(W_g)}{2(1-C\theta b_T)}
\right\}.
\tag{19}
\]
Multiplication of (19), exponential Markov inequality, and the choice
\(\theta\asymp b_T^{-1}\wedge h^d\operatorname{Var}(\sum_gW_g)^{-1}T\)
yield, for a deviation equal to a sufficiently small fixed multiple of \(Th^d\),
\[
P\left\{
\left|\sum_g(W_g-\mathbb EW_g)\right|>cTh^d
\right\}
\le C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right).
\tag{20}
\]
Adding the two parity bounds and the total-variation error (17) gives the same order for the full calendar sum.

For the Gram matrix, apply (20) to \(v^\top\Phi_{z,h}v\) on a fixed \(1/4\)-net \(\mathcal V\) of the unit sphere.  Its cardinality is fixed because \(q_r\) is fixed.  For every symmetric matrix \(A\), approximation of a maximizing eigenvector by an element of \(\mathcal V\) gives
\[
\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_{v\in\mathcal V}|v^\top Av|.
\tag{21}
\]
Equations (14)--(21) imply that, outside an event of probability at most
\[
C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right)+CT^{-A_0},
\tag{22}
\]
the calendar-level mass is at most \(2C_0Th^d\), while the calendar-level Gram matrix is at least \((c_0/2)Th^dI_{q_r}\).  Replication multiplies both by \(n_s\):
\[
L_s(h)=n_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell_{z,h}(X_{st}),
\qquad
G_s(h)=n_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st}).
\tag{23}
\]
Thus \(L_s(h)>0\) and
\[
\lambda_{\min}\{G_s(h)/L_s(h)\}
\ge c_0/(4C_0)>c_G
\]
outside (22).  Consequently,
\[
P\left\{L_s(h)=0\ \text{or}\
\lambda_{\min}\left(\frac{G_s(h)}{L_s(h)}\right)<c_G
\,\middle|\,E_0,\widetilde z_s\right\}
\le C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right)+CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{24}
\]
The finitely many small values of \(T\) are absorbed by enlarging \(C\).  No response variable and no upper-local-mass event occurs in (24).

Write \(h_0=h_{s,\beta}\).  If \(h_0<1\), its definition and a sufficiently large fixed \(C_h\) give
\[
\frac{T(2^vh_0)^d}{b_T}\ge c2^{vd}
\tag{25}
\]
for every dyadic candidate \(2^vh_0\le1\).  If selection has not stopped by that candidate, the candidate has failed.  Substitution of (25) into (24) proves
\[
P\{h_s>2^vh_{s,\beta}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s\}
\le C\exp(-c2^{vd})+CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{26}
\]
When \(h_0=1\), the assertion is immediate.  At the terminal candidate \(h=1\), (24) gives
\[
P\{\text{terminal-grid failure}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s\}
\le C\exp\{-cT/\log(T\vee2)\}+CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{27}
\]

Fix \(a>0\).  For the moment calculation only, repeat the total-variation comparison with a larger block multiplier so that its remainder is \(T^{-A_a}\) for some \(A_a>a/d+2\).  This changes neither the estimator nor its bandwidth grid; it changes only constants in (20)--(26), and the exponential dyadic tail remains summable.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[h_s^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s]
&\le h_0^a+
\sum_{v:\,2^vh_0<1}(2^{v+1}h_0)^a
P\{h_s>2^vh_0\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s\}\\
&\le Ch_0^a+CT^{-A_a}\\
&\le C\left\{(Tn_s)^{-a/(2\lambda+d)}
+\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right)^{a/d}
+N^{-a/2}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{28}
\]
Here \(\sum_{v\ge0}2^{av}e^{-c2^{vd}}<\infty\), the grid is capped at one, and \(h_0\ge c\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{1/d}\) absorbs \(T^{-A_a}\).

There is one selected fit per cohort.  A union bound over fixed \(S\) in (27) controls all selector failures.  The donor fourth-moment premise makes \(\bar Z\) and its projection finite almost surely; a successful normalized Gram matrix is invertible; and \(M_4(N)\), \(q_N\), and \(\delta_N\) are finite for every positive \(N\).  Since fixed \(D\) and \(\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}>0\) imply \(q_N\le C\), one has \(\delta_N\le CN^{-1/2}\), so \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\) eventually.  For the finitely many preceding indices, the deterministic bad-event indicator is bounded by a constant multiple of \(R_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Moreover, since \(A_0>2\lambda/d+2\),
\[
e^{-cT/\log(T\vee2)}+T^{-A_0}
\le C\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}
=CR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{29}
\]
Thus \(P(\mathrm{bad}\mid E_0)\le CR_{\star,\beta}\) along every stated array.  Finally, directly from the maximum defining the initial scale,
\[
T\{(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\}^d
\quad\text{may be }O(1),
\qquad
Th_{s,\beta}^d\ge c\log(T\vee2).
\tag{30}
\]
The second relation, rather than a dense-local-site assumption, supplies (25).  This proves all assertions using geometric mixing of the design alone.

Put \(D=Sd\).  For any class member define, only for this proof,
\[
Y=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_1-z_0).
\]
The definitions of \(z_0\) and \(\Sigma\), together with positive definiteness from \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, imply
\(\mathbb E_P[YY^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Taking traces, applying Jensen's inequality to the nonnegative variable \(\|Y\|_2^2\), and using \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} give
\[
D^2=\{\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^2\mid E_0]\}^2
\le\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^4\mid E_0]\le B.
\tag{31}
\]
Thus \(B<D^2\) gives an empty class.  Fix henceforth \(B\ge D^2\), an admissible interior query, and one cohort \(s_*\) having fixed positive weight; hold all other cohorts fixed across the two laws.

For sufficiently small fixed \(c_p,c_L>0\), set
\[
L_T=\lfloor c_L\log(T\vee2)\rfloor\vee1,
\qquad
p_T=c_p\frac{L_T}{T},
\]
where \(c_L|\log\rho_0|<1\).  Since \(p_T\asymp(\log T)/T\) whereas \(\rho_0^{L_T}\asymp T^{-c_L|\log\rho_0|}\), decreasing \(c_p\) gives
\[
2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}
\tag{32}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Let \(A_T\) be a Euclidean ball centered at \(z_{0s_*}\), contained in \([0,1]^d\), and having Lebesgue measure \(p_T\).  The interior-path condition permits this choice for large \(T\), and its radius satisfies
\[
h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}
\asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{1/d}.
\tag{33}
\]

Partition the calendar into deterministic consecutive blocks of length \(L_T\), apart from a final shorter block.  Independently across blocks draw \(G_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Conditional on \(G_b=1\), draw the selected cohort's design points in block \(b\) independently and uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(G_b=0\), draw them independently and uniformly on \([0,1]^d\setminus A_T\).  At each time the marginal density is
\[
p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
+(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1.
\tag{34}
\]
The other cohorts may be independent uniform designs.  Hence \texttt{ass:design-density} holds because \(c_X\le1\le C_X\).  At lags at least \(L_T\), the two relevant sigma-fields involve independent block variables.  At a smaller lag, only the block crossing the separating cut can be shared.  Conditional on that shared Bernoulli variable, the two sides are independent; expanding the two-component mixture bounds its absolute-regularity distance from the product law by \(2p_T(1-p_T)\le2p_T\).  Since \(\rho_0^\ell\ge\rho_0^{L_T-1}\) for \(1\le\ell<L_T\), (32) implies
\[
\beta_P(\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\mid E_0)
\le
\begin{cases}
2p_T,&1\le\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}<L_T,\\
0,&\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\ge L_T,
\end{cases}
\le\beta_0\rho_0^{\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}}.
\tag{35}
\]

Choose a bounded H\"older carrier \(g\) lying in the interior of the response range.  Give its weighted cohort surface a nonzero affine component at \(z_0\) when \(\lambda>1\), and an asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp there when \(0<\lambda\le1\); fixed scaling places the carrier inside the H\"older and two-sided-modulus envelopes.  Let \(\psi\) be a fixed smooth bump supported on the unit ball with \(\psi(0)=1\), and define in cohort \(s_*\)
\[
m_0(x)=g(x),
\qquad
m_1(x)=g(x)+c_bh_T^\lambda
\psi\left(\frac{x-z_{0s_*}}{h_T}\right).
\tag{36}
\]
Take \(c_b>0\) small enough that both surfaces remain in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) and in the response interior.  When \(\lambda>1\), the bump increment over a displacement of norm \(\delta\) is at most \(Cc_bh_T^{\lambda-1}\delta\) for \(\delta\le h_T\), and at most \(Cc_bh_T^\lambda\le Cc_bh_T^{\lambda-1}\delta\) for \(\delta>h_T\).  It therefore cannot cancel the fixed affine lower modulus.  When \(0<\lambda\le1\), the increment is at most \(Cc_b\delta^\lambda\), so it cannot cancel the carrier's cusp lower modulus when \(c_b\) is small.  The H\"older upper inequality and the covariance eigenvalue bounds give the upper standardized modulus.  Thus both laws obey \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} with \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

Conditional on the complete design \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,t\le T\}\), draw bounded historical response paths independently across units from kernels having mean \(m_\ell(X_{st})\); these kernels may vary by unit.  Draw bounded event outcomes independently of \(\mathscr X\) with a common mean under the two laws, and complete untreated event potential outcomes so that their cohort-average conditional means are \(m_\ell(z_{0s})\).  Then
\[
\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{37}
\]
For the donors use, under both laws, independent copies of
\[
Z_j=z_0+U_j,
\qquad
U_j\sim\operatorname{Unif}\{\pm\sqrt D\,e_k:1\le k\le D\},
\]
independently of the panel.  Symmetry gives
\[
\mathbb E[U_j\mid E_0]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E[U_jU_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D,
\qquad
\mathbb E[\|U_j\|_2^4\mid E_0]=D^2\le B.
\tag{38}
\]
Thus \(\Sigma=I_D\), including at \(B=D^2\), and the donor data carry no information distinguishing the two laws.  Take \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  Set observed and historical potential outcomes according to consistency, make historical potential outcomes invariant to event treatment, and make every potential outcome invariant to other units' assignments.  Choose all random wealth values in a compact subinterval of \((0,B)\), so that the primitive buy-and-hold representation can be realized with a positive common initial wealth and returns strictly greater than \(-1\).  Equations (34)--(38) and these completions verify every member property of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), including support, exact coordinates, limited anticipation, no spillovers, event transport, and both full-design centering restrictions.

Let \(\mathcal A_T\) be the event that no calendar block is active.  Since the number of blocks is \(T/L_T+O(1)\),
\[
P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)
=(1-p_T)^{T/L_T+O(1)}\longrightarrow e^{-c_p}>0.
\tag{39}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T\), every selected-cohort design point lies outside \(A_T\), where the surfaces in (36) agree.  All remaining observed kernels are common, so the complete observed-data laws coincide on this event.  Therefore
\[
\int\min\{dP_{0,T},dP_{1,T}\}
\ge P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)\ge c>0.
\tag{40}
\]
The observed event mean is common, whereas event transport changes the selected cohort's untreated event mean by \(c_bh_T^\lambda\).  The identification equality in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and (33) give
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,T}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,T}}(z_0)|
\ge ch_T^\lambda
\asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\tag{41}
\]
For the finitely many \(T\) preceding (32), use a fixed interior ball and two sufficiently close bounded response kernels with positive affinity and fixed nonzero target separation; decreasing the common constant makes (40)--(41) valid for every positive \(T\).

For any estimator, the two events on which its error from the respective target is at least half the separation cover the sample space.  Integrating against the overlap measure in (40) yields conditional squared risk at least \(cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\).  Decreasing \(c_p\) makes the affinity in (39) exceed \(2\alpha+a_0\) for some \(a_0>0\).  A conditionally honest interval covers both target values on overlap measure at least \(a_0\); on that event its length is at least the separation in (41).  Its worst-case conditional expected length is therefore at least \(c_\alpha R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}\).  The chosen event path lies in \(\mathcal Z_+\), so its conditional query probability is one and hence at least \(c_X\).  This proves the lemma for every compatible envelope without an anti-clustering premise.

Set
\[
a:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
q:=\frac{2\lambda}{d}.
\]
Because \(\lambda>0\) and \(d>0\), one has \(a\in(0,1)\) and \(q>0\).  We first derive the weighted geometric--arithmetic mean inequality used below.  For \(u>0\), define
\[
\phi(u):=au+(1-a)-u^a.
\]
Then \(\phi(1)=0\) and
\[
\phi'(u)=a\bigl(1-u^{a-1}\bigr).
\]
Since \(a-1<0\), one has \(\phi'(u)<0\) for \(0<u<1\) and \(\phi'(u)>0\) for \(u>1\).  Hence \(u=1\) is a global minimizer and \(\phi(u)\geq0\).  Substituting \(u=x/y\) and multiplying by \(y>0\) proves
\[
x^a y^{1-a}\leq ax+(1-a)y,
\qquad x>0,\quad y>0.
\tag{1}
\]

The definitions of \(a\) and \(q\) give
\[
q(1-a)
=\frac{2\lambda}{d}\frac{d}{2\lambda+d}
=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
=a.
\tag{2}
\]
For each cohort \(s\), the positive integers \(T\) and \(n_s\) permit application of \((1)\) with \(x=n_s^{-1}\) and \(y=T^{-q}\).  Using \((2)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
&=n_s^{-a}T^{-a}\\
&=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-q})^{1-a}\\
&\leq a n_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
The declared cohort weights are positive and satisfy \(\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s=1\).  Therefore
\[
\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s^2
\leq \left(\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s\right)^2
=1.
\tag{4}
\]
Multiplying \((3)\) by \(\pi_s^2\), summing over \(s\), applying \((4)\), and invoking the definitions of \(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\) in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) yields
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\tag{5}
\]

For every positive integer \(T\), \(\log(T\vee2)\geq\log2>0\).  Since \(q>0\), the definition of \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\) in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) implies
\[
T^{-q}
\leq (\log2)^{-q}
\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{q}
=(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{6}
\]
Combining \((5)\) and \((6)\), and using \(cx+dy\leq(c+d)(x\vee y)\) for nonnegative \(c,d,x,y\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
&\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\\
&\leq \bigl\{a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\bigr\}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr)\\
&=C_{\lambda,d}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
where the final equality uses \(1-a=d/(2\lambda+d)\) and \(q=2\lambda/d\).  Moreover, \(0<\log2<1\), so \((\log2)^{-q}>1\) and
\[
C_{\lambda,d}=a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\geq a+(1-a)=1.
\tag{8}
\]

Let
\[
A:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
D_0:=A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
All rate components are positive by \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\).  Its definition of \(R_{\star,\beta}\), together with \((7)\) and \((8)\), gives
\[
D_0
\leq R_{\star,\beta}
=D_0\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq D_0\vee(C_{\lambda,d}A)
\leq C_{\lambda,d}D_0.
\tag{9}
\]
Thus
\[
R_{\star,\beta}
\asymp_{\lambda,d}
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}},
\]
with comparison constants \(1\) and \(C_{\lambda,d}\), uniformly over \(N,T,S\) and the positive replication counts.

Now suppose \(T\geq3\).  Then \(T\vee2=T\) and \(\log T\geq\log3>1\), whence
\[
T^{-q}
\leq \left(\frac{\log T}{T}\right)^q
=R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{10}
\]
Substitution of \((10)\) into \((5)\) yields
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
\tag{11}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(a\in(0,1)\).  Taking the maximum with the other components in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) proves the exact identity
\[
R_{\star,\beta}
=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{12}
\]

By \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\), \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}\).  Along any joint growth array, this channel is negligible relative to \(A\) exactly when
\[
N^{-\kappa}=o(A),
\]
and it dominates \(A\) exactly when
\[
A=o(N^{-\kappa}).
\]
Because \(\kappa>0\) and \(A>0\), the boundary relation \(N^{-\kappa}\asymp A\) is equivalent, after raising both sides to the power \(-1/\kappa\) and absorbing fixed comparison constants, to
\[
N\asymp A^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
These comparisons describe minimax phases only when a separate statistical theorem establishes \(R_{\star,\beta}\) as the sharp risk for the experiment; equations \((1)\)--\((12)\) are algebraic and do not establish that premise.

For the independent-design comparator, or under the separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition specified in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\), the delivered spacing component is
\[
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-q}.
\]
Equation \((5)\) then gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp}}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}.
\tag{13}
\]
Using the comparator definition of \(R_\star\) in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\), equation \((13)\) implies
\[
R_\star
=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}
=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]

Finally, \(\texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}\) states
\[
X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}.
\]
Thus the historical regression coordinate is observed without a measurement-error convolution, so no inversion of such a convolution is required.  Consistently, inspection of the exhaustive maximum defining \(R_{\star,\beta}\) in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) shows neither a deconvolution component nor a separate moving-Gram component.  The same definition uses \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).  If \(\lambda>1\), then \(\kappa=1\), and hence
\[
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}=N^{-1}.
\]
This proves every assertion.

It suffices to construct one admissible triangular array.  Fix
\[
H=0,\qquad p=S=d=1,\qquad \lambda=\kappa=1,
\qquad \pi_1=1,
\]
where the last equality is forced by the normalization of the single cohort
weight.  Choose
\[
B=16,\qquad c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1,
\qquad \delta_0=\frac14,\qquad
c_{\mathrm{mod}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}=1.
\]
Choose any fixed \(\beta_0>0\) and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\), take the H\"older
radius \(L\) large enough to contain the affine function below, choose the
uniform order-zero kernel
\[
K(u)={\bf 1}\{|u|\leq1\},
\]
and fix the normalized-shape threshold with \(0<c_G\leq1\).  Since
\(\lambda=1\), the definitions of \(r\), \(b_r\), and \(e_0\) give
\[
r=\lceil1\rceil-1=0,\qquad b_0(u)=e_0=1.
\]
Let \(E_0\) be constant, let \(z_0=1/2\), let
\(\mathcal Z_+=\{1/2\}\), and, for each positive integer \(T\), set
\[
n_1=N=T^2.
\]

We first construct the historical sample.  Write \(X_t=X_{1t}\), and let
\(X_1,\ldots,X_T\) be independent and uniformly distributed on
\([0,1]\).  Define
\[
m(x)=8+x-\frac12,
\qquad
Q_{1ti}=m(X_t)+\frac12U_{ti},
\]
where the variables \((U_{ti})_{t,i}\) are mutually independent Rademacher
variables and are independent of the complete design.  Because
\(m([0,1])=[15/2,17/2]\),
\[
7\leq Q_{1ti}\leq9\leq B,
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[Q_{1ti}\mid X_t=x,E_0]=m(x).
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:bounded-historical-wealth} and
\texttt{ass:historical-regression} hold.  The affine function \(m\) belongs
to \(\mathcal H_1(1,L)\) by the choice of \(L\), proving
\texttt{ass:holder-smoothness}.  The conditional density of every \(X_t\)
is one on \([0,1]\), so \texttt{ass:design-density} holds with the displayed
values of \(c_X\) and \(C_X\).  Independence over calendar time implies
\[
\beta_P(\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\mid E_0)=0
\leq\beta_0\rho_0^{\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}}
\qquad(\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\geq1),
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.  Finally set
\(X_{1t}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_t\), as required by
\texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}.

Independently of the historical sample, let
\[
Z_j=\frac12+V_j,
\]
where \(V_1,\ldots,V_N\) are independent Rademacher variables.  Then
\[
\mathbb E_P[Z_j\mid E_0]=z_0,\qquad
\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_j\mid E_0)=1,
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \lvert\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\rvert^4\mid E_0
\right]=1\leq B.
\]
These equalities verify the defining relation for \(z_0\),
\texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, and \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}; the
construction also verifies \texttt{ass:donor-replication} and, by the stated
independence, \texttt{ass:donor-independence}.  If
\(0<\delta\leq\delta_0\), every \(z_0+u\) with \(|u|\leq\delta\) lies in
\([0,1]\).  Since \(\Sigma=1\), \texttt{def:local-modulus} therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\omega_P(\delta;z_0)
&=\sup_{|u|\leq\delta}|m(z_0+u)-m(z_0)|\\
&=\sup_{|u|\leq\delta}|u|=\delta.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} holds with
\(c_{\mathrm{mod}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}=1\).  Moreover,
\[
\operatorname{dist}(z_0,\partial[0,1])=\frac12\geq\delta_0,
\qquad
P\{z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\}=1\geq c_X,
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:interior-event-path} and
\texttt{ass:positive-query-region}.

We next specify the causal variables.  Define the design-measurable event
shock
\[
\Gamma={\bf 1}\{X_1\leq1/4\}
\]
and, for every \(i\), set
\[
B_{1i}(0)=8,\qquad B_{1i}(1)=8+\Gamma,
\qquad B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1).
\]
Define \(B_{1i}(a,\mathbf a_{-1i})=B_{1i}(a)\), and define
\(Q_{1ti}(a)=Q_{1ti}\) for both \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  These definitions verify,
respectively, \texttt{ass:consistency},
\texttt{ass:historical-consistency}, \texttt{ass:no-spillovers}, and
\texttt{ass:limited-anticipation}.  They also yield
\(0\leq B_{1i}(a)\leq9<B\), so \texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth} holds.
The construction is compatible with \texttt{def:buyhold-level}: take
\[
W_{1i,-1}=1,
\qquad
R_{1i0}(a)=B_{1i}(a)-1>-1;
\]
then \(W_{1i,-1}\{1+R_{1i0}(a)\}=B_{1i}(a)\).
Since \(m(z_0)=8\),
\[
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\mathbb E_P[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
=8=m(z_0),
\]
which is exactly \texttt{ass:event-transport}.  Conditional on the complete
design and \(E_0\), every event outcome is constant and the historical path
of unit \(i\) is a measurable function of
\((U_{ti})_{t=1}^T\).  The independence of these vectors across \(i\)
therefore gives \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}.  Together with the
preceding checks, every member property in \texttt{def:panel-law-class} is
satisfied, so the resulting law \(P_T\) belongs to
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(1)\).

The causal target is not the realized event mean.  Indeed, because \(z_0\)
and \(E_0\) are constant and \(P(\Gamma=1)=1/4\),
\texttt{def:target} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_n(z_0)
&=\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
  \mathbb E_P[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]\\
&=\mathbb E_P[\Gamma]=\frac14,
\end{aligned}
\qquad
\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}=8+\Gamma.
\]

We now analyze \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  Its generated and projected
centers are
\[
\bar Z=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^N Z_j,
\qquad
\widetilde z=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\bar Z).
\]
Metric projection onto \([0,1]\) fixes \(z_0\) and cannot increase distance
from \(z_0\).  Therefore, using independence and
\(\mathbb E[V_j]=0\), \(\mathbb E[V_j^2]=1\),
\[
|\widetilde z-z_0|
\leq\left|\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^NV_j\right|,
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde z-z_0)^2\mid E_0]
\leq\frac1N=T^{-2}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\), the initial bandwidth is below one and,
because \(n_1=N=T^2\), equals
\[
\underline h_T
=C_h\left[(Tn_1)^{-1/3}
\vee\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\vee N^{-1/2}\right]
=C_h\frac{\log T}{T}.
\]
Define
\[
I_T=\{t:|X_t-\widetilde z|\leq\underline h_T\},
\qquad
\mathcal A_T=\{|I_T|>0\}.
\]
For every fixed \(\widetilde z\in[0,1]\), the Lebesgue measure of
\([\widetilde z-\underline h_T,\widetilde z+\underline h_T]\cap[0,1]\)
is at least \(\underline h_T\).  Donor independence and the independent
uniform design thus imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0,\widetilde z)
&\leq(1-\underline h_T)^T\\
&\leq\exp(-T\underline h_T)=T^{-C_h}.
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, \(P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\to0\).

On \(\mathcal A_T\), the local mass and order-zero Gram matrix at the first
candidate satisfy
\[
L_1=n_1|I_T|,\qquad G_1=n_1|I_T|,
\qquad \lambda_{\min}(G_1/L_1)=1\geq c_G.
\]
Thus the selector accepts the initial candidate, and its least-squares
intercept is
\[
\widehat m_1
=\frac1{n_1|I_T|}
  \sum_{t\in I_T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Q_{1ti}.
\]
Its conditional-mean component differs from \(m(z_0)=8\) by at most
\[
\frac1{|I_T|}\sum_{t\in I_T}|m(X_t)-m(z_0)|
\leq\underline h_T+|\widetilde z-z_0|.
\]
Conditional on the design and donors, the Rademacher component has mean zero
and variance
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(
\frac1{2n_1|I_T|}\sum_{t\in I_T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}U_{ti}
\,\middle|\,(X_t)_{t=1}^T,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N,E_0
\right)
=\frac1{4n_1|I_T|}\leq\frac1{4n_1}.
\]
At every successful order-zero candidate the fitted intercept is an average
of observations in \([7,9]\); if all candidates fail, its defined value is
zero.  Hence \((\widehat m_1-8)^2\leq64\) on
\(\mathcal A_T^c\).  Combining this bound with the preceding bias and
variance calculations, for a fixed finite constant \(C\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_1-8)^2\mid E_0]
&\leq C\left\{
\underline h_T^2+N^{-1}+n_1^{-1}
+P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)
\right\}\\
&\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(D_T=\widehat m_1-m(z_0)\).  The displayed target calculation and the
definition of \(\widehat\tau\) imply the exact decomposition
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)=\Gamma-\frac14-D_T.
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left|
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
-\mathbb E_P[(\Gamma-1/4)^2\mid E_0]
\right|\\
&\quad\leq
2\{\mathbb E_P[(\Gamma-1/4)^2\mid E_0]\}^{1/2}
 \{\mathbb E_P[D_T^2\mid E_0]\}^{1/2}
+\mathbb E_P[D_T^2\mid E_0]
\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(\Gamma\) is Bernoulli with success probability \(1/4\),
\[
\lim_{T\to\infty}
\mathbb E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0\right]
=\operatorname{Var}_P(\Gamma)
=\frac14\left(1-\frac14\right)=\frac3{16}.
\]

For this array, the four iid-comparator components in
\texttt{def:rate-frontier} are
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}=n_1^{-1}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sm}}=(Tn_1)^{-2/3}=T^{-2},
\]
\[
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}=T^{-2}.
\]
Therefore \(R_\star=T^{-2}\), proving the first assertion.

It remains to analyze \texttt{def:honest-interval}.  On \(\mathcal A_T\),
the successful local-constant weights are
\[
a_{1ti}=\frac{{\bf 1}\{t\in I_T\}}{n_1|I_T|},
\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^T|a_{1ti}|=\frac1{n_1},
\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}|a_{1ti}|=1.
\]
For each fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), substitution into the two Hoeffding
radii yields
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}}\right)
\frac1{n_1}\right\}^{1/2}=O(T^{-1}),
\]
\[
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}}\right)
\frac1{n_1}\right\}^{1/2}=O(T^{-1}).
\]
The support of \(K\), nonnegativity of the weights, and their unit total
mass give
\[
A_L
\leq C_{0,1}L\underline h_T
=O\!\left(\frac{\log T}{T}\right).
\]
Here \(D=Sd=1\), so the exact donor calibration gives
\[
M_4(N)=\frac{16}{N}+3\left(1-\frac1N\right)\leq16,
\qquad
